text:
devon: paging alert — seeing p99 decode tail jump on streaming in us-west-2 since the nightly TRT/FlashAttn kernel push. p95 looks okay but p99s spiking to ~6s from baseline ~1.2s. affecting live streaming and some dedicated pools. paging @oncall

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: INC-20260310-8742 — Kernel compatibility regression affecting streaming decode latency. Severity: P2. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-8742

mira: looking at the metric dashboard now. live tail shows spikes aligned exactly with kernel-2026-03-10-trt8 build rollout at 02:11 UTC. p99 ingest -> 6200ms, p95 -> 1300ms. streaming stalls (stalling on decode loop, token emission delay).

alex: which models/populations? any customers complaining?

devon: primarily impacts large-context models (redwood-med-13b, opt-30b variants) on the TRT backend. A couple of customers in prod reported slow streaming (CS ticket #CS-4491). No global outage but SLOs breached for affected routes.

sam: throwing logs from the affected machine:

```
[03-10T02:18:33Z] decode: kernel compiled with -O3 -fuse-kernels=true
[03-10T02:18:33Z] trt: allocation hits fallback path, KV cache swipe -> pagefaults
[03-10T02:18:34Z] streaming: emit loop delayed 1500ms
```

lia: looks like the new compile flags are enabling an optimized kernel that regresses some memory access pattern -> more pagewalks on hosts with mixed GPU memory pressure.

mira: I reproduced locally with a canary image. When I toggle the flag `--enable-fuse` on the runtime it's fine, but enabling the new kernel binary causes the stall. Repro steps: `./run_canary.sh --model redwood/med-13b --kernel kernel-2026-03-10-trt8`

alex: mitigation options? rollback kernel, pin routes to older kernel, or route to dynamic fallback (cpu/old-trt) for streaming?

devon: short list: 1) roll back kernel-2026-03-10-trt8 from infra (fastest) 2) set routing override to kernel:trt7-stable for streaming routes (no deploy) 3) enable more aggressive prefix caching to reduce decode load temporarily 4) scale dedicated pool to absorb bursts (costly)

mira: rollback looks low-risk and fastest. ops-bot, any blockers on kernel rollbacks?

ops-bot: rollback pipeline exists. ETA ~7m to push kernel-rollback job to affected fleets. Confirm target: kernel-2026-03-09-trt7-stable. Will create rollback change and attach to INC-8742.

sam: adding a temporary routing override in the control plane now to pin streaming routes to trt7 while rollback propagates:

```
redwoodctl route update --route streaming-prod --set kernel=trt7-stable --duration 30m
```

lia: I also enabled a temporary KV-prefix cache for high-TPS routes (30s TTL) to reduce repeated decode pressure.

devon: pinging CS: lia, can you post a short customer note for CS-4491 and any customers on dedicated pools? say we're rolling back kernel and expect latency recovery in ~15m.

lia: on it. Draft: "We're investigating increased token latency in streaming for some models in us-west-2 after a kernel update. We're rolling back the kernel and applying routing overrides; expected recovery within 15-30 minutes. We'll follow up when SLOs are back to normal."

mira: rollback started (job id rb-8742-01). I'll watch kernel rollout logs. If rollback fails on any host, we'll add those hosts to a mitigation group and route away.

incident-bot: Update INC-8742: Action=rollback started by mira at 02:23 UTC. Status=in progress.

alex: monitoring traces — I can already see p99 trending down on a subset of hosts where rollback completed (02:28 UTC). p99 dropped from ~6.2s -> ~1.4s.

devon: good. continue to observe for 2x p99 windows and let’s keep routing override for 30m then reassess. Also create a postmortem ticket and tag eng-runtime + eng-sre for kernel test improvements.

mira: rollback finished across 95% of fleet at 02:34 UTC. Remaining hosts are draining and will switch in next 3-5m. Performing quick heap/kv sanity checks.

ops-bot: Rollback job rb-8742-01 completed: success on 112/118 hosts. 6 hosts failed (network timeout). Those 6 are isolated and have routing exceptions applied.

sam: outstanding action: re-run the compile regression tests with memory-pressure sims and flashattn flags. Also add a canary that exercises long-context streaming at scale before rolling future kernel builds.

lia: CS updated customers, sent CS-4491 note and flagged dedicated customers for direct follow-up.

devon: handoff summary for next oncall (alex): INC-8742 — kernel-2026-03-10-trt8 caused p99 streaming stalls in us-west-2. Mitigation: rolled back to trt7-stable, routing override applied to streaming-prod for 30m, KV-prefix cache enabled. Most hosts healthy; 6 hosts need manual rollback/network attention (ticket INF-8820). Expected SLO recovery; monitor p95/p99 and streaming stalls for next 1h.

alex: taking handoff. I'll keep watch on alerts and verify INF-8820 hosts. If p99 drifts up again, escalate to eng-runtime+build team and consider disabling `--enable-fuse` kernel flag in build pipeline until QA confirms.

incident-bot: INC-8742 updated: state=mitigated (partial) at 02:41 UTC. Next steps: postmortem, build-flag gating, improved canary. Assigned to devon/mira/sam.

devon: thanks team. tagging this thread for the postmortem. closing oncall thread — handoff to alex. :thumbsup:
